rows.grounds: instrumental of manner; compound describing dissolution of gross form
accusative goal; compound expressing identity with blazing awareness

items.question: What is regarded as the supreme offering in the Bhairava tradition?
premises: Entities suddenly and forcibly lose their gross form by being burned up.
By their own nature they attain unity with the blazing light of great awareness.
This attainment of unity with awareness-light is identified as the supreme offering in the Bhairava tradition.
items.inference: The supreme offering is the sudden dissolution of gross forms into the blazing light of awareness.
items.plain_english: Surely, when their gross form is suddenly burned away, things forcibly attain unity with the great blazing light of awareness by their very nature; this is regarded as the supreme offering in the Bhairava tradition.

rows.grounds: locative compound; awareness as sacrificial fire
object, refers to the fire of awareness

items.question: Why do entities offered into the fire of awareness kindle that fire?
premises: Entities properly offered by method into the fire within one's own awareness abandon division and difference.
By their own power those same entities kindle that fire of awareness.
The abandonment of difference and the kindling occur together in the act of offering.
items.inference: Entities offered into awareness both lose their separateness and intensify the fire of awareness by their own power.
items.plain_english: When entities are properly offered by method into the fire within one's own awareness, they abandon the division of difference and, by their own power, kindle that very fire.

rows.grounds: object created; elided initial vowel in sandhi
predicate verb; compound with infinitive-like dative sense

items.question: What becomes fit for meditation in this system of manifestation?
premises: By its own will and by the force of the nature of creation, consciousness manifests a sense-object in front.
Whatever sense-object is thus manifested becomes available for meditation.
Meditation is grounded in what is freely manifested, not in an abstract formlessness alone.
items.inference: Any sense-object freely manifested by the creative nature of consciousness is fit to serve as an object of meditation.
items.plain_english: Whatever sense-object consciousness creates before itself by its own will and by the force of its creative nature becomes fit for meditation on that very object.

rows.grounds: fused compound with instrumental sense of 'as'; subject of clause

items.question: Why is a particular form established as an object of meditation within formless consciousness?
premises: The abode of consciousness is formless yet consists of all forms.
Those who seek specific results require a determinate focus for meditation.
Therefore some particular form is established as the object of meditation for such seekers.
items.inference: Within formless, all-form consciousness, a particular form is posited as the meditation object for result-seeking practitioners.
items.plain_english: For although the abode of consciousness is formless and yet made of all forms, for those who seek results some particular form is established as the object of meditation.

rows.grounds: explanatory particle, sandhi form of hi
concessive particle, sandhi form of api

items.question: How can a particular form be sought within a nondual fullness?
premises: Reality is nondual and full, yet practical action still occurs within it.
A person fetching water sets aside other forms and seeks a pot.
The selection of a particular form does not negate the underlying fullness.
items.inference: Seeking a particular form within nondual fullness is analogous to choosing a pot to fetch water without denying the fullness of reality.
items.plain_english: Just as, even within a nondual and full reality, someone fetching water eagerly seeks a pot by setting aside other forms, so too a particular form may be chosen.

items.question: What causes a particular form to generate a particular conception of result?
premises: The supreme Lord's restrictive unfolding operates within the fullness of consciousness.
Through that unfolding, some particular form becomes salient.
That particular form gives rise to a corresponding conception of a specific result.
items.inference: The Lord's self-restriction makes a particular form produce a particular conception of fruit for the practitioner.
items.plain_english: In the same way, through the unfolding of the supreme Lord's self-restriction, some particular form gives rise to some particular conception of a result.

rows.grounds: relative subject, sandhi form of yaḥ

items.question: What kind of meditation unfolds for one who desires no particular result?
premises: Some practitioners act from the fullness of consciousness rather than from desire for a result.
Such a practitioner does not wish for any specific fruit.
For that person, meditation naturally takes the form of all forms at all times.
items.inference: One established in full consciousness experiences meditation as the spontaneous unfolding of all forms, without restriction to a particular object.
items.plain_english: But for one whose activity is the fullness of consciousness and who desires no result at all, meditation in the form of the whole universe unfolds at all times.

rows.grounds: genitive of subject, sandhi form of kulayoginaḥ
emphatic particle, sandhi form of api

items.question: How does experience arise for a Kula yogin intoxicated by the Bhairava essence?
premises: The Kula yogin reels from the intoxicant of the surging Bhairava essence.
In that state, experiences arise spontaneously and unpredictably.
Whatever arises, and in whatever manner it arises, is part of that reeling absorption.
items.inference: For the Kula yogin intoxicated by Bhairava essence, any experience arises spontaneously in whatever form it takes.
items.plain_english: For the Kula yogin reeling from the intoxicant of the surging Bhairava essence, whatever arises, in whatever way it arises, simply arises.

items.question: What is recognized as the seal in the unsurpassed teaching?
premises: A bodily absorption arises whose nature is delight and melting.
This absorption takes the whole world as its seal.
In the unsurpassed teaching, that world-embracing absorption is identified as the true seal.
items.inference: The true seal in the unsurpassed teaching is the bodily absorption of delight and melting that embraces the world.
items.plain_english: The bodily absorption whose nature is delight and melting is, in the unsurpassed teaching, the seal that has taken the whole world as its seal.

rows.grounds: emphatic particle, sandhi form of api

items.question: In whose heart does this rare method of yoga abide?
premises: This method of yoga abides in the heart of only some rare person.
It becomes present when the wheel of consciousness becomes clear.
Such clarity arises quickly for one who is in his final birth.
items.inference: This yoga method abides in the heart of a rare person whose consciousness-wheel clears, especially one nearing final birth.
items.plain_english: This rare method of yoga abides in the heart of someone whose wheel of consciousness becomes clear, quickly, as in the case of one who is in his final birth.

rows.grounds: present passive participle with instrumental agent
concessive particle, sandhi form of api

items.question: What happens to one in whom this yoga has matured, even while still embodied?
premises: Such a person may still be seen by ordinary people and remain in the condition of bodily bondage.
When yoga has matured in him, his state changes inwardly.
He attains an extraordinary awareness in an instant.
items.inference: Even while outwardly embodied and observed, one in whom yoga has matured instantly attains a special awareness.
uncertainties: The phrase 'na kṣaṇāt kām api saṃvidam' is syntactically compressed; the sense taken is that he attains an incomparable awareness in a moment.
items.plain_english: Even while being seen by people and remaining in the condition of bodily bondage, when yoga has matured he attains in an instant an incomparable awareness.

rows.grounds: contrastive particle, sandhi form of tu

items.question: What did the earlier teachers affirm about this state of yoga?
premises: The earlier teachers considered this very yogic state.
They strongly affirmed a specific consequence of it.
That consequence is the non-presence of the delusions of worldly experience.
items.inference: The earlier teachers held that in this yoga the delusions of worldly experience cease to be present.
items.plain_english: But right here, the intellect of our earlier teachers strongly affirmed the non-presence of the delusions of worldly experience.

rows.grounds: instrumental plural compound listing rival systems
instrumental plural compound listing other scriptural systems

items.question: What is the stance toward rival philosophical and scriptural systems in this context?
premises: Multiple rival systems are enumerated, including Vedic, Samkhya, dualist, logical, Buddhist, worldly, Pancaratra, ritual, and Siddhanta views.
The verse dismisses further engagement with them.
The dismissal implies they are insufficient for the matter at hand.
items.inference: For the present yogic realization, reliance on these rival philosophical and scriptural systems is unnecessary.
items.plain_english: Enough with the Vedic, Samkhya, dualist, logical, Buddhist, and worldly views, and with Pancaratra, ritual scriptures, Siddhanta, and the rest.

items.question: How do practitioners of different systems operate within their own frameworks?
premises: Different practitioners cultivate portions of knowledge and action suited to them.
They are established in their own respective procedures.
They act according to what is fitting within those procedures.
items.inference: Each system's adherents function coherently within their own procedures according to their own sense of appropriateness.
items.plain_english: All those various practitioners, cultivating the fitting portions of knowledge and action and established in their own procedures, act according to what is appropriate for them.

rows.grounds: subject; compound describing ritual/agricultural metaphorical sequence
predicate adjective; sandhi form of ativistṛtaḥ

items.question: What extensive preparatory process was carried out in the Shambhava branches?
premises: A sequence of acts such as sowing, implanting, and digging was performed.
This sequence was carried out by many branches of the Shambhava teaching.
The process was very extensive.
items.inference: The Shambhava tradition developed an extensive preparatory sequence of practices across its many branches.
uncertainties: The agricultural imagery (sowing, implanting, digging) may be metaphorical for spiritual preparation; taken literally in gloss and metaphorically in sense.
items.plain_english: Where the very extensive sequence of acts such as sowing, implanting, and digging was carried out by the many branches of the Shambhava teaching.

rows.grounds: instrumental plural compound describing ascetic marks

items.question: What is the unsurpassed fruit of the extensive Shambhava process?
premises: The prior extensive Shambhava process is likened to cultivating a tree of consciousness-Bhairava.
That cultivation yields a fruit.
The fruit is identified as unsurpassed, beyond external observances from life-stage duties to ascetic marks.
items.inference: The unsurpassed fruit of the Shambhava cultivation is the realization of consciousness-Bhairava, not mere external observances.
items.plain_english: The unsurpassed fruit of that tree of consciousness-Bhairava is this, beyond practices such as life-stage observances and even ascetic marks like matted hair and ointments.

rows.grounds: concessive particle, sandhi form of api

items.question: What happens to worldly pageantry for those resting in this yoga beyond ritual difference?
premises: In this state, no difference is found between acts done and acts not done.
Practitioners come to rest in that yoga.
For those resting there, the pageantry of worldly existence loses its hold.
items.inference: For those who rest in the yoga where done and undone make no difference, the pageantry of worldly existence dissolves.
items.plain_english: Where no difference is found between what is done and what is not done, for those who rest in that very yoga the pageantry of worldly existence dissolves.

rows.grounds: demonstrative in locative absolute, sandhi form of asmin

items.question: Why does worldly existence dissolve when one savors the nectar of awareness?
premises: Worldly existence is compared to a mass of snow in the great summer.
When the juicy nectar of awareness is savored, a transformative condition is present.
Under that condition, worldly existence melts away by itself.
items.inference: Savoring the nectar of awareness causes worldly existence to dissolve spontaneously, like snow in summer heat.
items.plain_english: Like a mass of snow in the great summer, it melts away by itself; for when this juicy nectar of awareness is savored, that is enough.

rows.grounds: locative compound referring to the author/work context
emphatic particle, sandhi form of api

items.question: How fully are the countless raptures of this realization presented here?
premises: Great raptures flow forth from this realization in countless numbers.
Their manifestations were already explained at length previously.
In this treatment by Abhinavagupta, only some of them are determined and set forth.
items.inference: Although the raptures of this realization are innumerable and previously detailed, only a few are definitively presented here.
uncertainties: The compound 'atrābhinavagupte' may refer to Abhinavagupta's present exposition or to a context within his teaching; taken as a locative reference to his treatment here.
items.plain_english: Great raptures flow forth, of which there is no number; their manifestations were already set out at length before, but here in Abhinavagupta's treatment only some are definitively stated.

rows.grounds: emphatic particle, sandhi form of api

items.question: Who is capable of delighting in the worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava?
premises: In the fragrance of the ketaki flower, the bee is the true connoisseur, not the fly.
The worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava is similarly subtle and discriminating.
One deluded by duality cannot delight in it, but a rare fit person can.
items.inference: Only a rare connoisseur, not one deluded by duality, delights in the worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava.
items.plain_english: In the rich fragrance of the ketaki flower, the bee alone is the connoisseur, not the fly; likewise, in the worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava, some rare one delights, not one deluded by duality.

rows.grounds: optative of as, sandhi form of syāt

items.question: Why is no purification required for one established in this realization?
premises: For one established in this state, no purification needs to be performed anywhere.
The world is understood as having Bhairava as its very nature.
If the world is Bhairava in nature, nothing in it can be truly impure.
items.inference: Because the world is of the nature of Bhairava, no purification is necessary for one established in that realization.
items.plain_english: For one established here, no purification of any kind would need to be done anywhere; for what in the world, whose very nature is Bhairava, could be impure?

rows.grounds: concessive particle, sandhi form of api

items.question: What logical problem arises if one tries to purify an allegedly impure mass of beings?
premises: If the mass of beings is taken as impure, some means of purification must be proposed.
Any proposed purifier would itself require justification or purification.
This leads to infinite regress and futile mutual dependence.
items.inference: Attempting to purify an allegedly impure world produces infinite regress and futile mutual dependence.
items.plain_english: And even if the mass of beings were impure, by what means could purification be effected? In that way there would be infinite regress and likewise a futile mutual dependence.

rows.grounds: demonstrative subject, sandhi form of tat
explanatory particle, sandhi form of hi

items.question: Why is purity not an independent reality if it depends on removing impurity?
premises: If impurity is concealed or removed, what is called purity also dissolves.
That shows purity is constituted by opposition to impurity.
What depends on an opposite is not established by its own nature, unlike blue.
items.inference: Purity is not an intrinsic nature but a relative designation dependent on the opposition of impurity.
items.plain_english: When the impure is concealed, what is called the pure dissolves as well; for that is constituted by its opposite and is not established by its own nature, like blue.

rows.grounds: concessive particle, sandhi form of api
genitive of the realized person; compound
past passive participle; sandhi of eva + ucchalitā

items.question: Why is there no insistence on grasping or rejecting sense objects for one established in supreme Bhairava consciousness?
premises: Purity and impurity are not intrinsic realities but relative designations.
For one whose nature is supreme Bhairava consciousness, sense objects do not bind by their own status.
Enjoyership surges forth spontaneously from that consciousness itself.
items.inference: Because enjoyership arises spontaneously from supreme Bhairava consciousness, there is no insistence on either grasping or rejecting sense objects.
items.plain_english: Therefore there is no insistence at all on either grasping or rejecting sense objects; for one whose nature is the consciousness of supreme Bhairava, enjoyership surges forth by itself.
